turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Tan. How are you feeling after the surgery?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: I'm okay, doctor. A bit tired, but not too bad.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's good to hear. Can you tell me your pain level out of 10? Any discomfort at the incision site or elsewhere?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Maybe a 4 or 5, mostly at the hernia site. It's manageable, I think.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Alright. Have you felt any nausea or dizziness since waking up? Any issues with vomiting?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, no nausea. I feel fine that way. Just a bit thirsty, actually.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Good. How about your breathing? Any shortness of breath or discomfort from the LMA during the procedure?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, I don't remember much, but I didn't wake up choking or anything. My throat feels a bit sore, but it's mild.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: That's expected sometimes with the LMA. We'll monitor that. Any recollection of the surgery itself?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No, nothing at all. I was out completely, which is good.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Excellent. Since you have a history of hypertension and diabetes, we'll keep an eye on your vitals and sugar levels. Any chest pain, dizziness, or urinary difficulty from BPH?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: No chest pain, and I went to the toilet before surgery, so I think I'm okay for now. My knees are aching a bit, but that's usual.

turns.speaker: PROVIDER
turns.text: Understood. We'll keep you comfortable and monitor everything. Let the nurse know if anything changes, okay?

turns.speaker: PATIENT
turns.text: Will do, doctor. Thanks for checking on me.
